Aptabase | Privacy-first analytics for mobile and desktop apps

summary.one_liner: Aptabase is an open-source, privacy-first analytics platform for mobile, desktop and web apps, offered as a managed cloud service or self-hosted.
summary.what_it_does: Aptabase provides usage analytics for apps, positioned as an open-source alternative to Firebase and Google Analytics. It offers SDKs for many frameworks, including Swift, Android (Kotlin), React Native, Flutter, Tauri, NativeScript, .NET MAUI, Electron, web apps, Unreal Engine and Unity. The README says it collects minimal usage data without unique identifiers, and focuses on monitoring sessions. It includes a built-in dashboard for essential metrics. The README says the server code and SDKs are fully open source, and that it aims to comply with GDPR, CCPA and PECR. Users can run it on their own servers or use the managed cloud version.
use_cases: track usage of a mobile app
session monitoring for Electron or Tauri apps
how_to_run: Self-hosting instructions are linked from the README ("Learn how"); no commands are given in the README itself
Managed Cloud option available as a hosted service
notable: Privacy-first design that avoids unique identifiers and tracks sessions instead
Wide SDK coverage across mobile, desktop, web and game engines
Server code and SDKs are fully open source
Managed cloud and self-hosted deployment options
Inspired by Plausible, per the README credits
caveats: Self-hosting means you are responsible for maintenance and updates
The managed cloud is a paid-or-free hosted service; README says only that a free trial is offered
Server code is licensed AGPLv3, which requires sharing modifications
keywords: measure how people use my app
